question: Does a crop drawn on the stage come back as the crop that was kept?

versions.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 2025-02-06-git-6da82b4485-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers

notes: offscreen; a 1920x1080 source in a 900x560 pane, so the stage is letterboxed and a mapping against the widget rect is wrong by a measurable amount
RUN WITH --broken: `_box` works the mapping out a second time against its own rect. `roundtrip` is expected to FAIL.
stage: overlay tracks the stage through a resize and a change of aspect; last stage PySide6.QtCore.QRect(8, 117, 434, 325)
maps: PySide6.QtCore.QRect(48, 61, 261, 171) out of the overlay maps to (86, 64, 566, 372) in source pixels

roundtrip: crop (130, 108, 784, 458) drawn at PySide6.QtCore.QRect(61, 56, 368, 237), and at PySide6.QtCore.QRect(61, 28, 368, 119) once the pane was halved — a box that did not move is one being mapped against something that did not either
gesture: a click sets nothing, a drag off the picture stops at its edge, a refused one says ['drawing a crop needs the whole frame on the stage — show it, then drag the rectangle']
closes: a drag set (32, 26, 1888, 498); typing a width of 3840 came back as 1888 in one push
stage (one answer to where the picture is): 4 checked, 0 disagreed

roundtrip (the box is the crop): 3 checked, 2 disagreed; first: the box is drawn at PySide6.QtCore.QRect(61, 56, 368, 237) and the crop it claims to be is at PySide6.QtCore.QRect(68, 81, 361, 211) — 26px out, which is the two mappings having become two implementations
